functions.name: xQueueGenericCreateStatic
functions.signature: QueueHandle_t xQueueGenericCreateStatic( const UBaseType_t uxQueueLength, const UBaseType_t uxItemSize, uint8_t * pucQueueStorage, StaticQueue_t * pxStaticQueue, const uint8_t ucQueueType );
functions.description: Internal generic static creator for queues and queue-based objects using caller-supplied storage.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 at build time.
pxStaticQueue must be a valid pointer to the control structure storage.

If uxItemSize != 0 then pucQueueStorage must be at least uxQueueLength * uxItemSize bytes; for semaphores (item size 0), storage pointer rules depend on object type; documentation specifies that item storage may be NULL if uxItemSize is 0.
ucQueueType must match queueQUEUE_TYPE_* values.
Returns NULL if pxStaticQueue is NULL or on failure; caller must check.

functions.name: xQueueGenericGetStaticBuffers
functions.signature: BaseType_t xQueueGenericGetStaticBuffers( QueueHandle_t xQueue, uint8_t ** ppucQueueStorage, StaticQueue_t ** ppxStaticQueue );
functions.description: Internal generic accessor to retrieve the static buffers used by a statically created queue or queue-based object.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 at build time.
xQueue must be a statically created queue/object.
ppucQueueStorage and ppxStaticQueue must be valid output pointers.
Returns pdTRUE on success; pdFALSE otherwise.

functions.name: xQueueCreateSet
functions.signature: QueueSetHandle_t xQueueCreateSet( const UBaseType_t uxEventQueueLength );
functions.description: Creates a queue set to allow a task to block on multiple queues/semaphores simultaneously using dynamic allocation.
requirements: configUSE_QUEUE_SETS and configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 at build time.
uxEventQueueLength specifies the maximum number of pending events the set can hold; to avoid lost events, it should be at least the sum of lengths/capacities described in the documentation examples.

functions.name: xQueueCreateSetStatic
functions.signature: QueueSetHandle_t xQueueCreateSetStatic( const UBaseType_t uxEventQueueLength, uint8_t * pucQueueStorage, StaticQueue_t * pxStaticQueue );
functions.description: Creates a queue set using caller-supplied storage.

pucQueueStorage must point to a buffer large enough for uxEventQueueLength events.
pxStaticQueue must point to a StaticQueue_t for the control structure; function returns NULL if pxStaticQueue is NULL.
uxEventQueueLength defines max events.

functions.name: xQueueAddToSet
functions.signature: BaseType_t xQueueAddToSet( QueueSetMemberHandle_t xQueueOrSemaphore, QueueSetHandle_t xQueueSet );
functions.description: Adds a queue or semaphore to an existing queue set.
requirements: configUSE_QUEUE_SETS must be 1 at build time.
xQueueOrSemaphore must be a valid queue/semaphore handle not already a member of another queue set.
xQueueSet must be a valid queue set handle.
A receive/take must not be performed on a member unless xQueueSelectFromSet has returned that member (usage constraint).
Returns pdPASS on success; pdFAIL if already a member of a different set.

functions.name: xQueueRemoveFromSet
functions.signature: BaseType_t xQueueRemoveFromSet( QueueSetMemberHandle_t xQueueOrSemaphore, QueueSetHandle_t xQueueSet );
functions.description: Removes a queue or semaphore from a queue set.
requirements: configUSE_QUEUE_SETS must be 1 at build time.
xQueueOrSemaphore must be a member of xQueueSet and must be empty to be removable.
Returns pdPASS on success; pdFAIL if not a member or not empty.

functions.name: xQueueSelectFromSet
functions.signature: QueueSetMemberHandle_t xQueueSelectFromSet( QueueSetHandle_t xQueueSet, const TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Blocks up to xTicksToWait to select a member of the queue set that is ready (queue has data or semaphore is available). Returns the ready member handle, or NULL on timeout.

xQueueSet must be a valid queue set handle.

functions.name: xQueueSelectFromSetFromISR
functions.signature: QueueSetMemberHandle_t xQueueSelectFromSetFromISR( QueueSetHandle_t xQueueSet );

requirements: configUSE_QUEUE_SETS must be 1 at build time.
May be called from an ISR context.
xQueueSet must be a valid queue set handle.
After it returns a member, the receive/take operation should target that member.

functions.name: uxQueueGetQueueItemSize
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxQueueGetQueueItemSize( QueueHandle_t xQueue );
functions.description: Returns the item size in bytes for the specified queue (0 for semaphores).
requirements: xQueue must be a valid queue/semaphore handle.

functions.name: uxQueueGetQueueLength
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxQueueGetQueueLength( QueueHandle_t xQueue );
functions.description: Returns the configured length (capacity in items) of the specified queue.
requirements: xQueue must be a valid queue handle.

functions.name: vSemaphoreCreateBinary
functions.signature: void vSemaphoreCreateBinary(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore);
functions.description: Deprecated macro that creates a binary semaphore using the queue mechanism and immediately gives it so the first take succeeds. Use xSemaphoreCreateBinary() instead (which creates it in the 'empty' state). Returns the created handle via the xSemaphore lvalue variable; the variable may remain NULL on failure. Intended for task/ISR synchronization.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
Caller must pass an lvalue of type SemaphoreHandle_t; the macro assigns to it
After the call, the caller must check xSemaphore != NULL before use
Header inclusion requirement: include FreeRTOS.h before semphr.h (file-level requirement)
This macro internally gives the semaphore once, so the first take will pass

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateBinary
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateBinary(void);
functions.description: Creates a binary semaphore in the 'empty' state (must be given before it can be taken) using dynamically allocated memory. Returns a handle or NULL on allocation failure. Suitable for task/ISR synchronization.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
Caller must check the returned SemaphoreHandle_t for NULL before use
The created binary semaphore starts empty; caller must give before take
Header inclusion requirement: include FreeRTOS.h before semphr.h (file-level requirement)

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateBinaryStatic(StaticSemaphore_t *pxSemaphoreBuffer);
functions.description: Creates a binary semaphore in the 'empty' state using caller-supplied static storage. Returns a handle, or NULL if pxSemaphoreBuffer is NULL. Avoids dynamic allocation.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
pxSemaphoreBuffer must point to a valid StaticSemaphore_t; if NULL, function returns NULL
The created binary semaphore starts empty; caller must give before take
Caller must check the returned handle for NULL before use

functions.name: xSemaphoreTake
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreTake(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore, TickType_t xBlockTime);
functions.description: Attempts to take (obtain) a semaphore (binary, counting, or mutex). Blocks up to xBlockTime ticks for availability. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE on timeout.
requirements: xSemaphore must be a valid handle created by xSemaphoreCreateBinary(), xSemaphoreCreateMutex(), or xSemaphoreCreateCounting()
Not for use from ISR; use xSemaphoreTakeFromISR() in ISRs
xBlockTime may be 0 to poll; portMAX_DELAY blocks indefinitely only if INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend == 1
If taking a mutex, ensure it will be given back once no longer required (priority inheritance)

functions.name: xSemaphoreTakeRecursive
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreTakeRecursive(SemaphoreHandle_t xMutex, TickType_t xBlockTime);
functions.description: Takes a recursive mutex. If the calling task already owns the mutex, the call succeeds immediately; ownership depth increases. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE on timeout.
requirements: configUSE_RECURSIVE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
xMutex must be a recursive mutex created with xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex()
Must not be used with mutexes created by xSemaphoreCreateMutex()
Each successful take must be matched by a corresponding xSemaphoreGiveRecursive() by the owning task
Not for use from ISR

functions.name: xSemaphoreGive
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreGive(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore);
functions.description: Releases (gives) a semaphore previously taken (binary, counting, or non-recursive mutex). Returns pdTRUE on success; pdFALSE if the semaphore could not be given (e.g., queue full, indicating misuse).
requirements: xSemaphore must refer to a semaphore created with xSemaphoreCreateBinary(), xSemaphoreCreateMutex(), or xSemaphoreCreateCounting()
Must not be called from ISR; use xSemaphoreGiveFromISR() in ISRs
Must not be used on recursive mutexes (use xSemaphoreGiveRecursive instead)
For mutexes, every take must be matched with a give to avoid priority inversion issues

functions.name: xSemaphoreGiveRecursive
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreGiveRecursive(SemaphoreHandle_t xMutex);
functions.description: Gives (releases) a recursive mutex previously taken recursively. Each give reduces the ownership depth; the mutex becomes available to other tasks when depth reaches zero. Returns pdTRUE on success.
requirements: configUSE_RECURSIVE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
xMutex must be a recursive mutex created with xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex()
Must not be used with mutexes created by xSemaphoreCreateMutex()
Not for use from ISR
Number of gives by the owner must match the number of successful takes

functions.name: xSemaphoreGiveFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreGiveFromISR(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore, BaseType_t *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken);
functions.description: Gives a semaphore from an interrupt service routine. If giving unblocks a higher-priority task, *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken is set to pdTRUE so the ISR can request a context switch. Returns pdTRUE on success; otherwise errQUEUE_FULL.
requirements: xSemaphore must be a binary or counting semaphore; must not be a mutex (xSemaphoreCreateMutex/xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex)
May be called from ISR context
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer if the caller wants to know if a context switch is required; the value may be set to pdTRUE
If *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken is set to pdTRUE, a context switch should be requested before exiting the ISR

functions.name: xSemaphoreTakeFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreTakeFromISR(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore, BaseType_t *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken);
functions.description: Takes a semaphore from an interrupt service routine. Typically used with counting semaphores when an ISR consumes a resource. If a higher-priority task is unblocked, *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken is set to pdTRUE. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: xSemaphore must be a binary or counting semaphore; must not be a mutex
May be called from ISR context
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer if the caller needs to determine if a context switch is required
This is an uncommon pattern; ensure it matches your design intent (e.g., ISR obtaining from a resource pool)

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateMutex
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateMutex(void);
functions.description: Creates a mutex semaphore using dynamic memory with priority inheritance. Use xSemaphoreTake()/xSemaphoreGive() to acquire/release. Returns handle or NULL on allocation failure. Not ISR-safe.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 and configUSE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
Must not be used from ISR
Do not use xSemaphoreTakeRecursive()/xSemaphoreGiveRecursive() with this mutex
Every take must be matched by a give

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateMutexStatic(StaticSemaphore_t *pxMutexBuffer);
functions.description: Creates a mutex semaphore using caller-supplied static storage with priority inheritance. Use xSemaphoreTake()/xSemaphoreGive(). Returns handle or NULL if pxMutexBuffer is NULL. Not ISR-safe.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 and configUSE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
pxMutexBuffer must point to a valid StaticSemaphore_t; if NULL, returns NULL
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
Must not be used from ISR
Do not use recursive take/give with this mutex
Every take must be matched by a give

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutex(void);
functions.description: Creates a recursive mutex using dynamic memory with priority inheritance. Must be used with xSemaphoreTakeRecursive()/xSemaphoreGiveRecursive(). Returns handle or NULL on allocation failure. Not ISR-safe.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 and configUSE_RECURSIVE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
Must not be used from ISR
Use only xSemaphoreTakeRecursive()/xSemaphoreGiveRecursive() with this mutex
Every take must be matched by a give (matching depth)

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutexStatic
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateRecursiveMutexStatic(StaticSemaphore_t *pxMutexBuffer);
functions.description: Creates a recursive mutex using caller-supplied static storage with priority inheritance. Use only the recursive take/give APIs. Returns handle or NULL if pxMutexBuffer is NULL. Not ISR-safe.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 and configUSE_RECURSIVE_MUTEXES must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
pxMutexBuffer must point to a valid StaticSemaphore_t; if NULL, returns NULL
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
Must not be used from ISR
Use only xSemaphoreTakeRecursive()/xSemaphoreGiveRecursive() with this mutex
Every take must be matched by a give (matching depth)

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateCounting
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateCounting(UBaseType_t uxMaxCount, UBaseType_t uxInitialCount);
functions.description: Creates a counting semaphore using dynamic memory. The count represents available events/resources. Returns a handle or NULL on allocation failure.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
uxInitialCount should be less than or equal to uxMaxCount (inferred from counting semaphore semantics)
Choose initial count according to use-case: 0 for event counting, max for resource pools

functions.name: xSemaphoreCreateCountingStatic
functions.signature: SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphoreCreateCountingStatic(UBaseType_t uxMaxCount, UBaseType_t uxInitialCount, StaticSemaphore_t *pxSemaphoreBuffer);
functions.description: Creates a counting semaphore using caller-supplied static storage. Returns a handle or NULL if pxSemaphoreBuffer is NULL.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
pxSemaphoreBuffer must point to a valid StaticSemaphore_t; if NULL, returns NULL
Caller must check returned handle for NULL before use
uxInitialCount should be less than or equal to uxMaxCount (inferred from counting semaphore semantics)

functions.name: vSemaphoreDelete
functions.signature: void vSemaphoreDelete(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore);
functions.description: Deletes a semaphore or mutex and frees its resources. Must be used with care; do not delete a mutex that is currently held.
requirements: xSemaphore must be a valid handle to a created semaphore/mutex
Do not delete a mutex while it is held by any task
Consider system state: deleting a semaphore that tasks are blocked on may have side effects (unspecified in this header)

functions.name: xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder
functions.signature: TaskHandle_t xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder(SemaphoreHandle_t xMutex);
functions.description: Returns the current holder task of a mutex, or NULL if xMutex is not a mutex or the mutex is not held. Value may become stale immediately after return.
requirements: configUSE_MUTEXES must be 1 and INCLUDE_xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
xMutex should be a mutex handle; returns NULL otherwise
Returned task handle is transient; do not rely on it remaining the holder

functions.name: xSemaphoreGetMutexHolderFromISR
functions.signature: TaskHandle_t xSemaphoreGetMutexHolderFromISR(SemaphoreHandle_t xMutex);
functions.description: ISR-safe version returning the current holder task of a mutex, or NULL if xMutex is not a mutex or is not held.
requirements: configUSE_MUTEXES must be 1 and INCLUDE_xSemaphoreGetMutexHolder must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
May be called from ISR context
xMutex should be a mutex handle; returns NULL otherwise

functions.name: uxSemaphoreGetCount
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxSemaphoreGetCount(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore);
functions.description: Returns the current count of a semaphore. For binary semaphores, returns 1 if available, 0 if not.
requirements: xSemaphore must be a valid semaphore handle (binary or counting)

functions.name: uxSemaphoreGetCountFromISR
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxSemaphoreGetCountFromISR(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore);
functions.description: ISR-safe function that returns the current count of a semaphore. For binary semaphores, returns 1 if available, 0 if not.
requirements: May be called from ISR context
xSemaphore must be a valid semaphore handle (binary or counting)

functions.name: xSemaphoreGetStaticBuffer
functions.signature: BaseType_t xSemaphoreGetStaticBuffer(SemaphoreHandle_t xSemaphore, StaticSemaphore_t **ppxSemaphoreBuffer);
functions.description: Retrieves the pointer to the static buffer used to hold the data structure of a statically created semaphore or mutex. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or this macro is unavailable
xSemaphore should refer to a statically created semaphore/mutex; dynamically created objects will not return a static buffer
ppxSemaphoreBuffer must be a valid pointer to receive the buffer pointer

functions.name: xEventGroupCreate
functions.signature: EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroupCreate( void );
functions.description: Creates a new FreeRTOS event group using dynamically allocated memory. Returns a handle to the created event group or NULL on allocation failure. Use this handle with other event group APIs.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1 at build time.
Must be called from task/RTOS context, not from an interrupt.
Caller must check the return value for NULL to handle allocation failure.

functions.name: xEventGroupCreateStatic
functions.signature: EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroupCreateStatic( StaticEventGroup_t * pxEventGroupBuffer );
functions.description: Creates a new FreeRTOS event group using application-supplied static storage. The provided StaticEventGroup_t buffer holds the event group’s internal data. Returns a handle or NULL if pxEventGroupBuffer is NULL.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1 at build time.
pxEventGroupBuffer must be a valid, writable pointer to a StaticEventGroup_t with correct size/alignment for the target port.
Must be called from task/RTOS context, not from an interrupt.
Caller must check the return value for NULL indicating invalid buffer.

functions.name: xEventGroupWaitBits
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupWaitBits( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToWaitFor, const BaseType_t xClearOnExit, const BaseType_t xWaitForAllBits, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Blocks the calling task until any or all of the specified event bits become set in the given event group, or until the timeout expires. Optionally clears the specified bits on exit. Returns the event group’s bits at the time of unblocking.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle created by xEventGroupCreate/xEventGroupCreateStatic.
Must not be called from an interrupt (ISR).
If xTicksToWait is portMAX_DELAY, INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend must be set to 1 at build time.
uxBitsToWaitFor specifies the bit mask to wait on; interpretation of xWaitForAllBits determines unblock condition.
If xClearOnExit is pdTRUE and the wait condition is met (not a timeout), the waited bits will be cleared before return.

functions.name: xEventGroupClearBits
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupClearBits( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToClear );
functions.description: Clears the specified bits in an event group. Returns the event group’s value prior to clearing. Not safe to call from an ISR.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle.
Must not be called from an interrupt (ISR).
uxBitsToClear is a bit mask indicating which bits to clear.

functions.name: xEventGroupClearBitsFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xEventGroupClearBitsFromISR( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToClear );
functions.description: ISR-safe request to clear bits in an event group by deferring the operation to the timer/daemon task. Returns pdPASS if the request was posted; pdFALSE if the timer service queue was full. If pdPASS is returned, a yield from ISR should be requested.
requirements: INCLUDE_xTimerPendFunctionCall must be 1 and configUSE_TIMERS must be 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle.
May be called from an ISR.
uxBitsToClear is a bit mask indicating which bits to clear.
If the function returns pdPASS, the ISR should call portYIELD_FROM_ISR(pdTRUE) to allow the timer task to run and perform the clear.

functions.name: xEventGroupSetBits
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupSetBits( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToSet );
functions.description: Sets the specified bits in an event group, potentially unblocking tasks waiting on those bits. Returns the event group’s value when the function returns (bits may have been auto-cleared if they unblocked waiters configured to clear on exit). Not ISR-safe.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle.
Must not be called from an interrupt (ISR).
uxBitsToSet is a bit mask indicating which bits to set.
Caller should not assume set bits remain set if setting them unblocked tasks that clear bits on exit.

functions.name: xEventGroupSetBitsFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xEventGroupSetBitsFromISR( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToSet, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: ISR-safe request to set bits in an event group by deferring the operation to the timer/daemon task. Returns pdPASS if the request was posted; pdFALSE if the timer service queue was full. Sets *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken to pdTRUE if a context switch should be requested before exiting the ISR.
requirements: INCLUDE_xTimerPendFunctionCall must be 1 and configUSE_TIMERS must be 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle.
May be called from an ISR.
uxBitsToSet is a bit mask indicating which bits to set.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid, writable pointer; it must be initialized to pdFALSE before the call.
If the function returns pdPASS and *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken is pdTRUE, the ISR should request a context switch using the port-specific macro (e.g., portYIELD_FROM_ISR).

functions.name: xEventGroupSync
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupSync( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, const EventBits_t uxBitsToSet, const EventBits_t uxBitsToWaitFor, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Atomically sets the specified bits, then waits for all bits in uxBitsToWaitFor to become set within the same event group, or until the timeout expires. Intended for task rendezvous/synchronization. On success, the waited bits are automatically cleared before return. Returns the event bits at the time of unblocking.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle created by xEventGroupCreate/xEventGroupCreateStatic.
Must not be called from an interrupt (ISR).
uxBitsToSet is a bit mask to set prior to waiting.
uxBitsToWaitFor is a bit mask; the function unblocks early only when all these bits are set, or timeout occurs.
On successful synchronization (not a timeout), the bits specified by uxBitsToWaitFor are cleared automatically before return.
xTicksToWait specifies the maximum block time in ticks.

functions.name: xEventGroupGetBits
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupGetBits( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup );
functions.description: Returns the current value of the bits in an event group. Note: In this header it is provided as a function-like macro that expands to xEventGroupClearBits(xEventGroup, 0), which performs no clearing but returns the event group value. Intended for use from task context (not from ISRs). Use when you need a snapshot of the event group’s bits without modifying them.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1.
Must not be called from an interrupt (ISR).
xEventGroup must be a valid event group handle previously created by xEventGroupCreate() or xEventGroupCreateStatic().
Returns the event group bits as they were when called; no bits are modified by this macro expansion.

functions.name: xEventGroupGetBitsFromISR
functions.signature: EventBits_t xEventGroupGetBitsFromISR( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup );
functions.description: Returns the current value of the event group’s bits when called from an ISR-safe context.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle.
May be called from an ISR.

functions.name: vEventGroupDelete
functions.signature: void vEventGroupDelete( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup );
functions.description: Deletes an event group created earlier. Any tasks blocked on the event group are unblocked and receive 0 as the event group’s value.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle created by the event group create APIs.
Must be called from task/RTOS context, not from an interrupt.

functions.name: xEventGroupGetStaticBuffer
functions.signature: BaseType_t xEventGroupGetStaticBuffer( EventGroupHandle_t xEventGroup, StaticEventGroup_t ** ppxEventGroupBuffer );
functions.description: Retrieves the pointer to the static buffer that backs a statically-created event group. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: configUSE_EVENT_GROUPS must be set to 1 at build time.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must be a valid handle to a statically created event group.
ppxEventGroupBuffer must be a valid pointer to receive the StaticEventGroup_t* result.

functions.name: uxEventGroupGetNumber
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxEventGroupGetNumber( void * xEventGroup );
functions.description: Returns a numeric identifier associated with the event group for trace/debug facilities. Only available when the trace facility is enabled. Exact semantics are trace-related.
requirements: configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must point to a valid event group object. Other usage constraints are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: vEventGroupSetNumber
functions.signature: void vEventGroupSetNumber( void * xEventGroup, UBaseType_t uxEventGroupNumber );
functions.description: Assigns a numeric identifier to the event group for trace/debug facilities. Only available when the trace facility is enabled. Exact semantics are trace-related.
requirements: configUSE_TRACE_FACILITY must be set to 1 at build time.
xEventGroup must point to a valid event group object.
uxEventGroupNumber is an application-defined value. Other usage constraints are not documented in this header (unknown).

functions.name: xStreamBufferCreate
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBufferCreate( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes );
functions.description: Create a stream buffer using dynamically allocated memory. Intended for one writer and one reader only. The trigger level controls when a task waiting for data is unblocked. Implemented as a macro that forwards to xStreamBufferGenericCreate.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or undefined.
xBufferSizeBytes specifies total capacity in bytes.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferCreateWithCallback
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBufferCreateWithCallback( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxSendCompletedCallback, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxReceiveCompletedCallback );
functions.description: Create a stream buffer (dynamic allocation) with custom send/receive completed callbacks. If a callback is NULL, the default sbSEND_COMPLETED/sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED macro behavior is used. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreate.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or undefined.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be set to 1 for this API to be available.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Callbacks run when data is sent/received as documented; passing NULL uses default macros.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferCreateStatic
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBufferCreateStatic( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, uint8_t * pucStreamBufferStorageArea, StaticStreamBuffer_t * pxStaticStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Create a stream buffer using statically supplied storage and control structure. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1.
pucStreamBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array of at least xBufferSizeBytes.
pxStaticStreamBuffer must point to a valid StaticStreamBuffer_t.
Returns NULL if either storage pointer is NULL.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferCreateStaticWithCallback
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBufferCreateStaticWithCallback( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, uint8_t * pucStreamBufferStorageArea, StaticStreamBuffer_t * pxStaticStreamBuffer, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxSendCompletedCallback, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxReceiveCompletedCallback );
functions.description: Create a stream buffer using static storage with custom send/receive completed callbacks. If a callback is NULL, the default completion macro is used. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be set to 1 for this API to be available.
pucStreamBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array of at least xBufferSizeBytes.
pxStaticStreamBuffer must point to a valid StaticStreamBuffer_t.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBatchingBufferCreate
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBatchingBufferCreate( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes );
functions.description: Create a stream batching buffer (dynamic allocation). Unlike a regular stream buffer, reads on a non-empty buffer will block until at least the trigger level of data is available (or timeout). Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreate with batching type.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or undefined.
xTriggerLevelBytes defines the amount of data required to unblock a reader before timeout.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBatchingBufferCreateWithCallback
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBatchingBufferCreateWithCallback( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxSendCompletedCallback, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxReceiveCompletedCallback );
functions.description: Create a stream batching buffer (dynamic allocation) with custom completion callbacks. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreate.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 or undefined.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be set to 1 for this API to be available.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBatchingBufferCreateStatic
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBatchingBufferCreateStatic( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, uint8_t * pucStreamBufferStorageArea, StaticStreamBuffer_t * pxStaticStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Create a statically allocated stream batching buffer using supplied storage and control structure. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1.
pucStreamBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array of at least xBufferSizeBytes.
pxStaticStreamBuffer must point to a valid StaticStreamBuffer_t.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBatchingBufferCreateStaticWithCallback
functions.signature: StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBatchingBufferCreateStaticWithCallback( size_t xBufferSizeBytes, size_t xTriggerLevelBytes, uint8_t * pucStreamBufferStorageArea, StaticStreamBuffer_t * pxStaticStreamBuffer, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxSendCompletedCallback, StreamBufferCallbackFunction_t pxReceiveCompletedCallback );
functions.description: Create a statically allocated stream batching buffer with custom completion callbacks. Implemented as a macro to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be set to 1 for this API to be available.
pucStreamBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array of at least xBufferSizeBytes.
pxStaticStreamBuffer must point to a valid StaticStreamBuffer_t.
xTriggerLevelBytes must be <= xBufferSizeBytes; 0 is treated as 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferGetStaticBuffers
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferGetStaticBuffers( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, uint8_t ** ppucStreamBufferStorageArea, StaticStreamBuffer_t ** ppxStaticStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Retrieve the pointers to a statically created stream buffer’s storage area and control structure that were supplied at creation time.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set to 1 for this symbol to be available.
xStreamBuffer must refer to a valid stream buffer (typically one created statically for meaningful results).
ppucStreamBufferStorageArea and ppxStaticStreamBuffer must be valid pointers to receive outputs.
Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise.

functions.name: xStreamBufferSend
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferSend( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, const void * pvTxData, size_t xDataLengthBytes, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Copy bytes from pvTxData into the stream buffer from task context, optionally blocking for space. Returns the number of bytes actually written.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from task context (use xStreamBufferSendFromISR in ISRs).
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pvTxData must point to at least xDataLengthBytes readable bytes.
xTicksToWait specifies maximum block time in ticks; use pdMS_TO_TICKS for ms conversion; portMAX_DELAY blocks indefinitely if INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend == 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferSendFromISR
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferSendFromISR( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, const void * pvTxData, size_t xDataLengthBytes, BaseType_t * const pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Interrupt-safe send: copy bytes into the stream buffer from ISR context. Returns the number of bytes written and indicates via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken if a higher-priority task was unblocked.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from ISR context (do not call from tasks).
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pvTxData must point to at least xDataLengthBytes readable bytes.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer and should be initialised to pdFALSE before the call; check it and request a context switch if set to pdTRUE.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferReceive
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferReceive( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, void * pvRxData, size_t xBufferLengthBytes, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Receive bytes from a stream buffer into pvRxData from task context, optionally blocking for data. Returns the number of bytes actually read.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from task context (use xStreamBufferReceiveFromISR in ISRs).
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pvRxData must point to a writable buffer of at least xBufferLengthBytes.
xTicksToWait specifies maximum block time in ticks; portMAX_DELAY blocks indefinitely if INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend == 1.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: xStreamBufferReceiveFromISR
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferReceiveFromISR( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, void * pvRxData, size_t xBufferLengthBytes, BaseType_t * const pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Interrupt-safe receive: copy bytes out of the stream buffer into pvRxData from ISR context. Returns the number of bytes read and indicates via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken if a higher-priority task was unblocked.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from ISR context (do not call from tasks).
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pvRxData must point to a writable buffer of at least xBufferLengthBytes.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer and should be initialised to pdFALSE before the call; check it and request a context switch if set to pdTRUE.
Only a single writer and a single reader may access the buffer concurrently; multiple writers/readers must be externally serialized.

functions.name: vStreamBufferDelete
functions.signature: void vStreamBufferDelete( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Delete a stream buffer created with dynamic or static allocation. Frees dynamically allocated memory. The handle must not be used after deletion.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle created previously.
After deletion, the handle becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: xStreamBufferIsFull
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferIsFull( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Query whether the stream buffer is full (no free space available). Returns pdTRUE if full, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.

functions.name: xStreamBufferIsEmpty
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferIsEmpty( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Query whether the stream buffer is empty (contains no data). Returns pdTRUE if empty, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.

functions.name: xStreamBufferReset
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferReset( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Reset a stream buffer to its initial empty state from task context, discarding any data. Fails if any task is blocked on the buffer to send or receive.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from task context (use xStreamBufferResetFromISR in ISRs).
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
No tasks may be blocked waiting to send to or receive from the buffer; otherwise the function returns pdFAIL.

functions.name: xStreamBufferResetFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferResetFromISR( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Interrupt-safe reset of a stream buffer to its initial empty state from ISR context, discarding any data. Fails if any task is blocked on the buffer to send or receive.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be called from ISR context.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
No tasks may be blocked waiting to send to or receive from the buffer; otherwise the function returns pdFAIL.

functions.name: xStreamBufferSpacesAvailable
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferSpacesAvailable( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Return the number of free bytes available to write before the stream buffer would be full.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.

functions.name: xStreamBufferBytesAvailable
functions.signature: size_t xStreamBufferBytesAvailable( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Return the number of bytes currently stored in the stream buffer that can be read before it would be empty.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.

functions.name: xStreamBufferSetTriggerLevel
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferSetTriggerLevel( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, size_t xTriggerLevel );
functions.description: Update the stream buffer’s trigger level, which controls when a task blocked waiting for data is unblocked. Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE if the level exceeds the buffer length.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
xTriggerLevel must be <= the buffer’s length. A value of 0 results in a trigger level of 1 being used.

functions.name: xStreamBufferSendCompletedFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferSendCompletedFromISR( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Advanced use: Notify a task that data was sent to the buffer, equivalent to the internal sbSEND_COMPLETED() behavior, from ISR context. Not for general use outside custom completion implementations.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be used only to implement a custom sbSEND_COMPLETED() equivalent; MUST NOT be used at other times.
Must be called from ISR context.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer initialised to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, request a context switch before exiting the ISR.
Returns pdTRUE if a task was unblocked, otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: xStreamBufferReceiveCompletedFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xStreamBufferReceiveCompletedFromISR( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Advanced use: Notify a task that data was read from the buffer, equivalent to the internal sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED() behavior, from ISR context. Not for general use outside custom completion implementations.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
Must be used only to implement a custom sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED() equivalent; MUST NOT be used at other times.
Must be called from ISR context.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer initialised to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, request a context switch before exiting the ISR.
Returns pdTRUE if a task was unblocked, otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: uxStreamBufferGetStreamBufferNotificationIndex
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxStreamBufferGetStreamBufferNotificationIndex( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer );
functions.description: Get the task notification index used by the stream buffer for its task notifications. Returns the current index, or the default if not changed.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.

functions.name: vStreamBufferSetStreamBufferNotificationIndex
functions.signature: void vStreamBufferSetStreamBufferNotificationIndex( StreamBufferHandle_t xStreamBuffer, UBaseType_t uxNotificationIndex );
functions.description: Set the task notification index the stream buffer will use for its notifications on subsequent API calls. Recommended to set before sending or receiving to avoid inconsistencies.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be set to 1.
xStreamBuffer must be a valid handle.
uxNotificationIndex must be a valid task notification index for the target port (exact range is platform-defined).
Call before using the buffer to avoid inconsistent notification indices.

functions.name: xMessageBufferCreate
functions.signature: MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBufferCreate( size_t xBufferSizeBytes );
functions.description: Create a new message buffer using dynamically allocated memory. Intended for task and ISR messaging with variable-length messages. This macro maps to xStreamBufferGenericCreate with sbTYPE_MESSAGE_BUFFER and no callbacks.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 (or undefined) in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xBufferSizeBytes is the total storage in bytes (payload + sizeof(size_t) per message).
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls (e.g., via critical sections and 0 block time).
Returns NULL on insufficient heap; on success returns a non-NULL handle.

functions.name: xMessageBufferCreateWithCallback
functions.signature: unknown (function-like macro; callback parameter types not declared in this header)
functions.description: Create a new message buffer (dynamic allocation) and register optional send/receive completion callbacks. This macro maps to xStreamBufferGenericCreate with sbTYPE_MESSAGE_BUFFER and the provided callbacks.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1 (or undefined) in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be 1 to enable callbacks; if NULL callbacks are provided, defaults defined by sbSEND_COMPLETED/sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED are used.
xBufferSizeBytes is the total storage in bytes (payload + sizeof(size_t) per message).
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.
Callback parameter types are not specified in this header; consult stream_buffer.h for the exact callback type signatures.

functions.name: xMessageBufferCreateStatic
functions.description: Create a message buffer using caller-supplied static storage for both the control structure and the storage area. This macro maps to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic with sbTYPE_MESSAGE_BUFFER and no callbacks.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
pucMessageBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array at least xBufferSizeBytes in size.
pxStaticMessageBuffer must point to a StaticMessageBuffer_t object.
Maximum storable payload is xBufferSizeBytes - 1 bytes (each message also incurs sizeof(size_t) overhead).
Returns NULL if pucMessageBufferStorageArea or pxStaticMessageBuffer is NULL; otherwise returns a valid handle.
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.

functions.name: xMessageBufferCreateStaticWithCallback
functions.signature: unknown (function-like macro; callback parameter types not declared in this header)
functions.description: Create a message buffer using static storage and register optional send/receive completion callbacks. This macro maps to xStreamBufferGenericCreateStatic with sbTYPE_MESSAGE_BUFFER and the provided callbacks.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
configUSE_SB_COMPLETED_CALLBACK must be 1 to enable callbacks; if NULL callbacks are provided, defaults defined by sbSEND_COMPLETED/sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED are used.
pucMessageBufferStorageArea must point to a uint8_t array at least xBufferSizeBytes in size.
pxStaticMessageBuffer must point to a StaticMessageBuffer_t object.
Maximum storable payload is xBufferSizeBytes - 1 bytes (each message also incurs sizeof(size_t) overhead).
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.
Callback parameter types are not specified in this header; consult stream_buffer.h for the exact callback type signatures.

functions.name: xMessageBufferGetStaticBuffers
functions.description: Retrieve the pointers to a statically created message buffer’s storage area and control structure buffers that were supplied at creation.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1.
xMessageBuffer must reference a statically created message buffer.
ppucMessageBufferStorageArea and ppxStaticMessageBuffer must be valid pointers to receive the returned addresses.
Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise.

functions.name: xMessageBufferSend
functions.description: Send a discrete message to a message buffer from a task context. Copies xDataLengthBytes from pvTxData into the buffer, also storing the message length internally.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid message buffer handle.
pvTxData must point to a buffer with at least xDataLengthBytes bytes.
Each message consumes xDataLengthBytes + sizeof(size_t) bytes of buffer space.
xTicksToWait is a block time in ticks; 0 means do not block; portMAX_DELAY waits indefinitely only if INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend == 1.
Returns 0 if timeout occurs before enough space is available; otherwise returns xDataLengthBytes.
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.

functions.name: xMessageBufferSendFromISR
functions.description: Interrupt-safe send of a discrete message to a message buffer. Copies xDataLengthBytes from pvTxData; may unblock a task waiting for data.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
Callable from ISR context.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid message buffer handle.
pvTxData must point to a buffer with at least xDataLengthBytes bytes.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must point to a BaseType_t variable initialized to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, a context switch should typically be requested before exiting the ISR.
Returns 0 if insufficient space; otherwise returns xDataLengthBytes.
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.

functions.name: xMessageBufferReceive
functions.signature:
size_t xMessageBufferReceive( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer,
                              void *pvRxData,
                              size_t xBufferLengthBytes,
                              TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Receive the next complete message from a message buffer into pvRxData from task context. If pvRxData is too small for the next message, the message is left in the buffer and 0 is returned.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid message buffer handle.
pvRxData must point to a buffer of length at least xBufferLengthBytes.
If xBufferLengthBytes is smaller than the next message, the message remains in the buffer and 0 is returned.
xTicksToWait is a block time in ticks; 0 means return immediately if empty; portMAX_DELAY waits indefinitely only if INCLUDE_vTaskSuspend == 1.
Returns the message length on success; returns 0 on timeout or if the next message exceeds xBufferLengthBytes.
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.

functions.name: xMessageBufferReceiveFromISR
functions.signature:
size_t xMessageBufferReceiveFromISR( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer,
                                     void *pvRxData,
                                     size_t xBufferLengthBytes,
                                     BaseType_t *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Interrupt-safe receive of the next complete message from a message buffer into pvRxData. May unblock a task waiting for space.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
Callable from ISR context.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid message buffer handle.
pvRxData must point to a buffer of length at least xBufferLengthBytes.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must point to a BaseType_t variable initialized to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, a context switch should typically be requested before exiting the ISR.
Returns the number of bytes copied (0 if no message was available or buffer too small for next message).
Single writer and single reader only; if multiple writers/readers exist, the application must serialize API calls.

functions.name: vMessageBufferDelete
functions.signature: void vMessageBufferDelete( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Delete a message buffer created via dynamic or static creation. Frees allocated memory for dynamically created buffers. After deletion, the handle must not be used.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle created by xMessageBufferCreate() or xMessageBufferCreateStatic().
A message buffer handle must not be used after it has been deleted.

functions.name: xMessageBufferIsFull
functions.signature: BaseType_t xMessageBufferIsFull( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Test whether the message buffer cannot accept any more messages of any size until space is freed.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
Returns pdTRUE if full, pdFALSE otherwise.

functions.name: xMessageBufferIsEmpty
functions.signature: BaseType_t xMessageBufferIsEmpty( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Test whether the message buffer contains no messages.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
Returns pdTRUE if empty, pdFALSE otherwise.

functions.name: xMessageBufferReset
functions.signature: BaseType_t xMessageBufferReset( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Reset the message buffer to its initial empty state from task context, discarding all messages.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
There must be no tasks blocked on the message buffer when resetting; otherwise the reset fails.
Returns pdPASS on success; pdFAIL if reset could not be performed due to blocked tasks.

functions.name: xMessageBufferResetFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xMessageBufferResetFromISR( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Interrupt-safe reset of the message buffer to its initial empty state, discarding all messages.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
Callable from ISR context.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
There must be no tasks blocked on the message buffer when resetting; otherwise the reset fails.
Returns pdPASS on success; pdFAIL if reset could not be performed due to blocked tasks.

functions.name: xMessageBufferSpaceAvailable
functions.signature: size_t xMessageBufferSpaceAvailable( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Return the number of free bytes currently available in the message buffer. Each message written also uses sizeof(size_t) bytes for its length header.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
Returned space reflects raw bytes; the largest payload that can be sent is returned_value - sizeof(size_t).

functions.name: xMessageBufferSpacesAvailable
functions.signature: size_t xMessageBufferSpacesAvailable( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Alias of xMessageBufferSpaceAvailable() that corrects a historical typo; returns the number of free bytes in the message buffer.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
Returned space reflects raw bytes; the largest payload that can be sent is returned_value - sizeof(size_t).

functions.name: xMessageBufferNextLengthBytes
functions.signature: size_t xMessageBufferNextLengthBytes( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer );
functions.description: Return the length in bytes of the next message pending in the buffer, or 0 if empty. Useful after a receive attempt returned 0 due to an undersized destination buffer.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
Returns 0 if the message buffer is empty.

functions.name: xMessageBufferSendCompletedFromISR
functions.signature:
BaseType_t xMessageBufferSendCompletedFromISR( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer,
                                               BaseType_t *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Advanced use only. Notify that data was sent to the message buffer from ISR context to unblock a task waiting for data, for custom implementations of sbSEND_COMPLETED(). Not to be used at any other time.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
Callable from ISR context only for implementing a custom sbSEND_COMPLETED() equivalent.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must point to a BaseType_t initialized to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, a context switch should typically be requested before exiting the ISR.
Returns pdTRUE if a task was unblocked; otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: xMessageBufferReceiveCompletedFromISR
functions.signature:
BaseType_t xMessageBufferReceiveCompletedFromISR( MessageBufferHandle_t xMessageBuffer,
                                                  BaseType_t *pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Advanced use only. Notify that data was read from the message buffer from ISR context to unblock a task waiting for space, for custom implementations of sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED(). Not to be used at any other time.
requirements: configUSE_STREAM_BUFFERS must be 1 in FreeRTOSConfig.h.
Callable from ISR context only for implementing a custom sbRECEIVE_COMPLETED() equivalent.
xMessageBuffer must be a valid handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must point to a BaseType_t initialized to pdFALSE before the call; if set to pdTRUE, a context switch should typically be requested before exiting the ISR.
Returns pdTRUE if a task was unblocked; otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: xTimerCreate
functions.signature: TimerHandle_t xTimerCreate( const char * const pcTimerName, const TickType_t xTimerPeriodInTicks, const BaseType_t xAutoReload, void * const pvTimerID, TimerCallbackFunction_t pxCallbackFunction );
functions.description: Creates a new software timer using dynamically allocated memory and returns its handle. The timer is created dormant; start or reset it to activate. Use when configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION == 1.
requirements: configSUPPORT_DYNAMIC_ALLOCATION must be 1.
xTimerPeriodInTicks must be > 0.
pxCallbackFunction must match TimerCallbackFunction_t: void (*)(TimerHandle_t).
Returned handle is NULL on allocation failure; callers must check for NULL before use.
May be called before the scheduler starts; created timer will start only after scheduler start when later started/reset.
pvTimerID is an opaque identifier retrievable via pvTimerGetTimerID().

functions.name: xTimerCreateStatic
functions.signature: TimerHandle_t xTimerCreateStatic( const char * const pcTimerName, const TickType_t xTimerPeriodInTicks, const BaseType_t xAutoReload, void * const pvTimerID, TimerCallbackFunction_t pxCallbackFunction, StaticTimer_t * pxTimerBuffer );
functions.description: Creates a new software timer using application-supplied storage and returns its handle. The timer is created dormant; start or reset it to activate. Use when avoiding dynamic allocation.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1.
xTimerPeriodInTicks must be > 0.
pxCallbackFunction must match TimerCallbackFunction_t: void (*)(TimerHandle_t).
pxTimerBuffer must point to valid StaticTimer_t storage for the timer; function returns NULL if pxTimerBuffer is NULL.
Callers must check the returned handle for NULL before use.
May be called before the scheduler starts; created timer will start only after scheduler start when later started/reset.
pvTimerID is an opaque identifier retrievable via pvTimerGetTimerID().

functions.name: pvTimerGetTimerID
functions.signature: void * pvTimerGetTimerID( const TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns the user-provided ID associated with a timer, set at creation or via vTimerSetTimerID(). Useful to disambiguate timers sharing a callback.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
Returns the current ID value; may be NULL if none was set.

functions.name: vTimerSetTimerID
functions.signature: void vTimerSetTimerID( TimerHandle_t xTimer, void * pvNewID );
functions.description: Sets or updates the user-provided ID associated with a timer. The value can later be read with pvTimerGetTimerID().
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.

functions.name: xTimerIsTimerActive
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerIsTimerActive( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns non-zero if the timer is active, or pdFALSE if dormant. Timers are dormant when created and after a one-shot timer expires until restarted.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.

functions.name: xTimerGetTimerDaemonTaskHandle
functions.signature: TaskHandle_t xTimerGetTimerDaemonTaskHandle( void );
functions.description: Returns the handle of the timer service/daemon task. Use to query task state or for diagnostics. Not valid before the scheduler starts.
requirements: Must not be called before the scheduler has started.

functions.name: xTimerStart
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerStart( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Starts a dormant timer or restarts an active timer (equivalent to reset), queuing a start command to the timer daemon. Implemented as a macro that wraps xTimerGenericCommand.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
configUSE_TIMERS must be 1.
xTicksToWait is the max time to wait to send the command to the timer queue; it is ignored if called before the scheduler starts.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.
The timer’s expiry will be relative to the time xTimerStart() is called (or scheduler start if called prior).

functions.name: xTimerStop
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerStop( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Stops an active timer by queuing a stop command to the timer daemon. Implemented as a macro that wraps xTimerGenericCommand.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
configUSE_TIMERS must be 1.
xTicksToWait is the max time to wait to send the command; ignored if called before the scheduler starts.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerChangePeriod
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerChangePeriod( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xNewPeriod, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Changes a timer’s period (active or dormant) and starts it if necessary, by queuing a change-period command to the timer daemon. Implemented as a macro that wraps xTimerGenericCommand.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
configUSE_TIMERS must be 1.
xNewPeriod must be > 0 and is specified in ticks.
xTicksToWait is the max time to wait to send the command; ignored if called before the scheduler starts.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerDelete
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerDelete( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Deletes a previously created timer by queuing a delete command to the timer daemon. Implemented as a macro that wraps xTimerGenericCommand.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle created with xTimerCreate or xTimerCreateStatic.
configUSE_TIMERS must be 1.
xTicksToWait is the max time to wait to send the command; ignored if called before the scheduler starts.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerReset
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerReset( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Resets a timer’s expiry relative to now (restarts if active; starts if dormant) by queuing a reset command to the timer daemon. Implemented as a macro that wraps xTimerGenericCommand.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
configUSE_TIMERS must be 1.
xTicksToWait is the max time to wait to send the command; ignored if called before the scheduler starts.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.
If called before the scheduler starts, the timer will start when the scheduler starts and expiry is relative to scheduler start.

functions.name: xTimerStartFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerStartFromISR( TimerHandle_t xTimer, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: ISR-safe version of xTimerStart(). Queues a start/reset command from interrupt context and optionally requests a context switch via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken.
requirements: Must be called from an interrupt context.
xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer; must be initialised to pdFALSE by the caller before the call; may be set to pdTRUE to request a context switch on ISR exit.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerStopFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerStopFromISR( TimerHandle_t xTimer, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: ISR-safe version of xTimerStop(). Queues a stop command from interrupt context and optionally requests a context switch via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken.
requirements: Must be called from an interrupt context.
xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer; must be initialised to pdFALSE by the caller before the call; may be set to pdTRUE to request a context switch on ISR exit.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerChangePeriodFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerChangePeriodFromISR( TimerHandle_t xTimer, TickType_t xNewPeriod, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: ISR-safe version of xTimerChangePeriod(). Queues a change-period command from interrupt context and optionally requests a context switch via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken.
requirements: Must be called from an interrupt context.
xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
xNewPeriod must be > 0 and is specified in ticks.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer; must be initialised to pdFALSE by the caller before the call; may be set to pdTRUE to request a context switch on ISR exit.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerResetFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerResetFromISR( TimerHandle_t xTimer, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: ISR-safe version of xTimerReset(). Queues a reset/start command from interrupt context and optionally requests a context switch via pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken.
requirements: Must be called from an interrupt context.
xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer; must be initialised to pdFALSE by the caller before the call; may be set to pdTRUE to request a context switch on ISR exit.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on command queued, pdFAIL otherwise.

functions.name: xTimerPendFunctionCallFromISR
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerPendFunctionCallFromISR( PendedFunction_t xFunctionToPend, void * pvParameter1, uint32_t ulParameter2, BaseType_t * pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken );
functions.description: Defers execution of a callback function to the timer daemon task from interrupt context. The function and parameters are queued for later execution in task context.
requirements: INCLUDE_xTimerPendFunctionCall must be 1.
Must be called from an interrupt context.
xFunctionToPend must match PendedFunction_t: void (*)(void *, uint32_t).
pxHigherPriorityTaskWoken must be a valid pointer; must be initialised to pdFALSE by the caller before the call; may be set to pdTRUE to request a context switch on ISR exit.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on message queued, otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: xTimerPendFunctionCall
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerPendFunctionCall( PendedFunction_t xFunctionToPend, void * pvParameter1, uint32_t ulParameter2, TickType_t xTicksToWait );
functions.description: Defers execution of a callback function to the timer daemon task from task context. The function and parameters are queued for later execution in task context.
requirements: INCLUDE_xTimerPendFunctionCall must be 1.
xFunctionToPend must match PendedFunction_t: void (*)(void *, uint32_t).
xTicksToWait specifies how long to block for space on the timer queue if full.
Caller must check the return value: pdPASS on message queued, otherwise pdFALSE.

functions.name: pcTimerGetName
functions.signature: const char * pcTimerGetName( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns the name assigned to a timer at creation time. Intended for diagnostics/debugging.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
Returned pointer is to internal storage; treat as read-only.

functions.name: vTimerSetReloadMode
functions.signature: void vTimerSetReloadMode( TimerHandle_t xTimer, const BaseType_t xAutoReload );
functions.description: Sets whether a timer is auto-reload (periodic) or one-shot. Auto-reload timers reset themselves on expiry; one-shot timers become dormant after expiry.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
xAutoReload should be pdTRUE for auto-reload or pdFALSE for one-shot.

functions.name: xTimerGetReloadMode
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerGetReloadMode( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns pdTRUE if the timer is configured as auto-reload, otherwise pdFALSE for one-shot.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.

functions.name: uxTimerGetReloadMode
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxTimerGetReloadMode( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns pdTRUE if the timer is configured as auto-reload, otherwise pdFALSE for one-shot. Same query as xTimerGetReloadMode but returns UBaseType_t.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.

functions.name: xTimerGetPeriod
functions.signature: TickType_t xTimerGetPeriod( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns the timer’s period in ticks.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.

functions.name: xTimerGetExpiryTime
functions.signature: TickType_t xTimerGetExpiryTime( TimerHandle_t xTimer );
functions.description: Returns the tick count at which the timer will next expire. If this value is less than the current tick count then the expiry time has overflowed. If the timer is not running the return value is undefined.
requirements: xTimer must be a valid timer handle.
Only meaningful if the timer is running; otherwise return value is undefined.

functions.name: xTimerGetStaticBuffer
functions.signature: BaseType_t xTimerGetStaticBuffer( TimerHandle_t xTimer, StaticTimer_t ** ppxTimerBuffer );
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the StaticTimer_t buffer used by a statically created timer.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be 1.
xTimer must refer to a timer that was created statically to retrieve a meaningful buffer pointer.
ppxTimerBuffer must be a valid pointer to receive the buffer address.
Returns pdTRUE on success, pdFALSE otherwise; caller must check the return value.

functions.name: vApplicationGetTimerTaskMemory
functions.signature: void vApplicationGetTimerTaskMemory( StaticTask_t ** ppxTimerTaskTCBBuffer, StackType_t ** ppxTimerTaskStackBuffer, configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE * puxTimerTaskStackSize );
functions.description: Application-provided hook used to supply static memory for the Timer (daemon) task’s TCB and stack when static allocation is enabled.
requirements: configSUPPORT_STATIC_ALLOCATION must be set (required).
ppxTimerTaskTCBBuffer must return a pointer to a valid StaticTask_t storage.
ppxTimerTaskStackBuffer must return a pointer to a valid StackType_t array for the timer task stack.
puxTimerTaskStackSize must return the number of StackType_t elements available in the provided stack buffer.
This function must be provided by the application when static allocation is enabled.

functions.name: vApplicationDaemonTaskStartupHook
functions.signature: void vApplicationDaemonTaskStartupHook( void );
functions.description: Optional application hook called once by the timer (daemon) task when it starts running. Use for initialization that should occur in the context of the daemon task.
requirements: configUSE_DAEMON_TASK_STARTUP_HOOK must be non-zero for the hook to be called.
If provided, the implementation must be non-blocking or bounded to avoid delaying the timer task.

functions.name: xCoRoutineCreate
functions.signature: BaseType_t xCoRoutineCreate( crCOROUTINE_CODE pxCoRoutineCode, UBaseType_t uxPriority, UBaseType_t uxIndex );
functions.description: Creates a new co-routine and adds it to the ready list. The co-routine entry point must be a function of type crCOROUTINE_CODE and use the co-routine macro protocol (crSTART/crEND, and blocking via cr* macros). Returns pdPASS on success, otherwise an error code defined in ProjDefs.h.
requirements: pxCoRoutineCode must be a valid function matching the crCOROUTINE_CODE prototype: void (*)(CoRoutineHandle_t xHandle, UBaseType_t uxIndex).
The co-routine function must use crSTART(xHandle) at its start and crEND() at its end.
Within the co-routine function, blocking/yielding must be performed using co-routine macros (e.g., crDELAY, crQUEUE_*), not task APIs.
uxPriority specifies the co-routine’s priority relative to other co-routines (range/limits are platform-specific and not stated here).
uxIndex is used to distinguish instances when multiple co-routines share the same function.
Check the return value: pdPASS indicates successful creation; otherwise handle the error code.

functions.name: vCoRoutineSchedule
functions.signature: void vCoRoutineSchedule( void );
functions.description: Runs the highest-priority co-routine that is able to run. Executes cooperatively until the co-routine blocks, yields, or is preempted by a task. In applications that use both tasks and co-routines, this should be called from the idle task (e.g., in the idle hook).
requirements: If both tasks and co-routines are used, call vCoRoutineSchedule() from the idle task hook (either once per idle hook invocation or in a loop per examples).
Do not expect co-routines to preempt each other; they are cooperative. Tasks can preempt co-routines.

functions.name: crSTART
functions.signature: #define crSTART( pxCRCB )
functions.description: Macro that must be invoked at the start of every co-routine function. It initializes the co-routine’s internal state machine (using the control block’s uxState) and sets up the switch-based resume point machinery required by co-routines.
requirements: Must be called as the first statement in every co-routine function body.
The argument pxCRCB must be the CoRoutineHandle_t (xHandle) passed to the co-routine function.
Variables that must retain values across blocking points in a co-routine must be declared static (as co-routines do not maintain their own stacks).
Only call co-routine blocking/yielding macros (e.g., crDELAY, crQUEUE_*) directly within the co-routine function body.

functions.name: crEND
functions.signature: #define crEND()
functions.description: Macro that must be invoked at the end of every co-routine function. It closes the switch started by crSTART and finalizes the co-routine state machine.
requirements: Must be the final macro call in every co-routine function body matching a preceding crSTART.
Do not place executable statements after crEND() in the co-routine function.

functions.name: crDELAY
functions.signature: #define crDELAY( xHandle, xTicksToDelay )
functions.description: Co-routine macro that delays the calling co-routine for a specified number of ticks. Internally places the co-routine onto a delayed list and yields using the co-routine state machine.
requirements: Must be called directly from within a co-routine function (not from a sub-function), because co-routines do not maintain their own stack.
xHandle must be the CoRoutineHandle_t passed to the co-routine function.
xTicksToDelay specifies the number of tick periods to delay; timing conversion depends on configTICK_RATE_HZ (use portTICK_PERIOD_MS to convert to ms).

functions.name: crQUEUE_SEND
