functions.signature: #define crQUEUE_SEND( xHandle, pxQueue, pvItemToQueue, xTicksToWait, pxResult )
functions.description: Co-routine macro equivalent of xQueueSend() for tasks. Attempts to send an item to a queue, optionally blocking (co-routine block) for up to xTicksToWait if the queue is full. Sets *pxResult to pdPASS on success, or an error code (e.g., errQUEUE_BLOCKED, errQUEUE_YIELD) as defined in ProjDefs.h.
requirements: Must be called directly from within a co-routine function (not from a sub-function).
xHandle must be the CoRoutineHandle_t for the calling co-routine.
pxQueue must be a valid QueueHandle_t previously created by xQueueCreate().
pvItemToQueue must point to a buffer containing an item of the size configured for the queue.
xTicksToWait is the maximum ticks to block waiting for space; timebase per configTICK_RATE_HZ (use portTICK_PERIOD_MS for ms).
pxResult must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; on return, *pxResult will be pdPASS on success or an error code defined in ProjDefs.h.
Caller must check *pxResult after the macro completes and handle non-pdPASS outcomes.

functions.name: crQUEUE_RECEIVE
functions.signature: #define crQUEUE_RECEIVE( xHandle, pxQueue, pvBuffer, xTicksToWait, pxResult )
functions.description: Co-routine macro equivalent of xQueueReceive() for tasks. Attempts to receive an item from a queue, optionally blocking (co-routine block) for up to xTicksToWait if the queue is empty. Copies the received item into pvBuffer and sets *pxResult to pdPASS on success, or an error code as defined in ProjDefs.h.
requirements: Must be called directly from within a co-routine function (not from a sub-function).
xHandle must be the CoRoutineHandle_t for the calling co-routine.
pxQueue must be a valid QueueHandle_t previously created by xQueueCreate().
pvBuffer must point to a buffer large enough for one queue item (size defined at queue creation).
xTicksToWait is the maximum ticks to block waiting for an item; timebase per configTICK_RATE_HZ (use portTICK_PERIOD_MS for ms).
pxResult must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; on return, *pxResult will be pdPASS on success or an error code defined in ProjDefs.h.
Caller must check *pxResult after the macro completes and handle non-pdPASS outcomes.

functions.name: crQUEUE_SEND_FROM_ISR
functions.signature: #define crQUEUE_SEND_FROM_ISR( pxQueue, pvItemToQueue, xCoRoutinePreviouslyWoken )
functions.description: ISR-safe macro for sending an item to a queue that is used by co-routines. Returns pdTRUE if a co-routine was unblocked by the send, enabling the ISR to decide if a context switch is required.
requirements: Must be called from an ISR context to send to a queue used by a co-routine.
pxQueue must be a valid QueueHandle_t.
pvItemToQueue must point to an item whose size matches the queue’s item size.

xCoRoutinePreviouslyWoken should be pdFALSE on the first call within an ISR; on subsequent calls within the same ISR, pass the value returned by the previous call to ensure at most one co-routine is woken.

functions.name: crQUEUE_RECEIVE_FROM_ISR
functions.signature: #define crQUEUE_RECEIVE_FROM_ISR( pxQueue, pvBuffer, pxCoRoutineWoken )
functions.description: ISR-safe macro for receiving an item from a queue that is used by co-routines. Copies the received item into pvBuffer. Returns pdTRUE if an item was received; if a co-routine is unblocked by the receive, *pxCoRoutineWoken is set to pdTRUE.
requirements: Must be called from an ISR context to receive from a queue used by a co-routine.
pxQueue must be a valid QueueHandle_t.
pvBuffer must point to a buffer large enough for one queue item (size defined at queue creation).
pxCoRoutineWoken must be a valid, non-NULL pointer; it may be set to pdTRUE if a co-routine is unblocked by the receive.

functions.name: vCoRoutineAddToDelayedList
functions.signature: void vCoRoutineAddToDelayedList( TickType_t xTicksToDelay, List_t * pxEventList );
functions.description: Internal co-routine support function used by macros to remove the current co-routine from the ready list and place it into the appropriate delayed list for xTicksToDelay ticks. If pxEventList is non-NULL, the co-routine may also be inserted into an event list.
requirements: Intended for internal use by the co-routine implementation only; application code should not call this directly.
xTicksToDelay is the number of ticks to delay the current co-routine (must be a valid TickType_t).
pxEventList may be NULL (as used by crDELAY) or point to a valid event List_t used for synchronization.

functions.name: xCoRoutineRemoveFromEventList
functions.signature: BaseType_t xCoRoutineRemoveFromEventList( const List_t * pxEventList );
functions.description: Internal queue/co-routine support function that removes the highest priority co-routine from the specified event list and places it into the pending ready list. Returns a status (BaseType_t) indicating the outcome per implementation.
requirements: Intended for internal use by the queue implementation only; application code should not call this directly.
pxEventList must be a valid pointer to a const List_t representing an event list containing co-routines.

functions.name: vCoRoutineResetState
functions.signature: void vCoRoutineResetState( void ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Resets the internal state of the co-routine module. Must be called by the application before restarting the scheduler to reinitialize co-routine state.
requirements: Must be called by the application before restarting the scheduler.
Function is marked PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION; call-site/privilege requirements depend on the port’s privilege model.
Should not be called while the scheduler is running (not stated explicitly, but implied by “before restarting the scheduler”).

functions.name: vListInitialise
functions.signature: void vListInitialise( List_t * const pxList ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Initialises a FreeRTOS list object. Sets up internal links and places a sentinel end marker so the list starts empty and ready for insert/remove operations. Use this before any other operation on the list.
requirements: pxList must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable List_t storage.
This function must be called before the list is used by any other list API.
The function sets pxList->xListEnd.xItemValue to portMAX_DELAY and initialises counters/links; callers should not rely on prior contents.

functions.name: vListInitialiseItem
functions.signature: void vListInitialiseItem( ListItem_t * const pxItem ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Initialises a list item so it can be safely inserted into a list. It clears the item's container pointer to indicate it is not currently in any list.
requirements: pxItem must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to writable ListItem_t storage.
Must be called before the item is inserted into any list.
After initialisation, pxItem->pxContainer is set to NULL; callers should set the item's xItemValue and pvOwner as appropriate before insertion.

functions.name: vListInsert
functions.signature: void vListInsert( List_t * const pxList, ListItem_t * const pxNewListItem ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Inserts a list item into a list in ascending order of the item's xItemValue. Typical use is to keep time or priority ordered lists in the scheduler.
requirements: pxList must be a valid, initialised list (vListInitialise must have been called).
pxNewListItem must be a valid, initialised list item (vListInitialiseItem must have been called).
pxNewListItem must not currently be contained in any list (pxNewListItem->pxContainer must be NULL).
Before calling, callers should set pxNewListItem->xItemValue to the sort key and pxNewListItem->pvOwner to the owning object as needed.

functions.name: vListInsertEnd
functions.signature: void vListInsertEnd( List_t * const pxList, ListItem_t * const pxNewListItem ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Inserts a list item into a list at the position such that it will be the last item returned by repeated listGET_OWNER_OF_NEXT_ENTRY iterations (effectively at the end relative to the list's pxIndex traversal).
requirements: pxList must be a valid, initialised list (vListInitialise must have been called).
pxNewListItem must be a valid, initialised list item (vListInitialiseItem must have been called).
pxNewListItem must not currently be contained in any list (pxNewListItem->pxContainer must be NULL).
Callers should set pxNewListItem->pvOwner as appropriate before insertion.

functions.name: uxListRemove
functions.signature: UBaseType_t uxListRemove( ListItem_t * const pxItemToRemove ) PRIVILEGED_FUNCTION;
functions.description: Removes a list item from the list that currently contains it, using the item's pxContainer pointer. Returns the number of items remaining in that list after the removal.
requirements: pxItemToRemove must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a ListItem_t that is currently contained within a list (pxItemToRemove->pxContainer must not be NULL).
The list from which the item is removed must be a valid, initialised list.
Callers should use the return value to know the remaining item count if needed; after removal, pxItemToRemove->pxContainer is set to NULL.

functions.name: pxPortInitialiseStack
functions.signature: StackType_t * pxPortInitialiseStack( StackType_t * pxTopOfStack, StackType_t * pxEndOfStack, TaskFunction_t pxCode, void * pvParameters, BaseType_t xRunPrivileged, xMPU_SETTINGS * xMPUSettings )
functions.description: Initializes a new task’s stack with the register/context frame expected by the port, ready for scheduling. This MPU-enabled, overflow-checking variant also receives the end-of-stack marker and MPU settings.
requirements: Only available when portUSING_MPU_WRAPPERS == 1 and portHAS_STACK_OVERFLOW_CHECKING == 1.
pxTopOfStack must point to the initial top of the task’s stack area.
pxEndOfStack must point to the end (limit) of the same stack area.
pxCode must be a valid TaskFunction_t entry point.
pvParameters is the parameter passed to the task function (may be NULL).
xRunPrivileged indicates privilege for the task; valid values are port-defined BaseType_t booleans.
xMPUSettings must point to writable storage to receive MPU config for the task.
Caller must ensure stack memory is correctly allocated and aligned for the port.
Must be called during task creation, before the task is scheduled.

functions.name: vPortDefineHeapRegions
functions.signature: void vPortDefineHeapRegions( const HeapRegion_t * const pxHeapRegions )
functions.description: Defines multiple heap regions (for heap_5) that together compose the FreeRTOS heap. The array of HeapRegion_t entries specifies start addresses and sizes and is terminated by an entry with size 0.
requirements: Must be called before any call to pvPortMalloc() (including implicit calls via creating tasks, queues, semaphores, mutexes, timers, event groups, etc.).
pxHeapRegions must point to an array of HeapRegion_t entries terminated by an entry whose xSizeInBytes == 0.
The region with the lowest start address must appear first in the array.
Each pucStartAddress must be valid and accessible RAM and sized per xSizeInBytes.
Do not call after the heap is in use.

functions.name: vPortGetHeapStats
functions.signature: void vPortGetHeapStats( HeapStats_t * pxHeapStats )
functions.description: Fills a HeapStats_t structure with statistics about the current heap state (free space, largest/smallest free block, allocation/free counts, etc.).
requirements: pxHeapStats must point to writable storage for a HeapStats_t.
Heap must be initialized/configured prior to calling.

functions.name: pvPortMalloc
functions.signature: void * pvPortMalloc( size_t xWantedSize )
functions.description: Allocates a block of memory of xWantedSize bytes from the FreeRTOS heap implementation for the port.
requirements: xWantedSize specifies the size in bytes to allocate.
Returned pointer must be freed with vPortFree().
Allocation may fail; callers must handle failure (e.g., NULL return) and note that vApplicationMallocFailedHook() may be called if configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK == 1.

functions.name: pvPortCalloc
functions.signature: void * pvPortCalloc( size_t xNum, size_t xSize )
functions.description: Allocates zero-initialized memory for an array of xNum elements of xSize bytes each using the FreeRTOS heap implementation for the port.
requirements: xNum is the element count; xSize is bytes per element.
Returned pointer must be freed with vPortFree().
Allocation may fail; callers must handle failure (e.g., NULL return) and note that vApplicationMallocFailedHook() may be called if configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK == 1.

functions.name: vPortFree
functions.signature: void vPortFree( void * pv )
functions.description: Frees a block of memory previously allocated by pvPortMalloc/pvPortCalloc (or pvPortMallocStack when enabled) back to the FreeRTOS heap.
requirements: pv must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by a matching FreeRTOS heap allocation routine for this port.
Do not free memory not obtained from the FreeRTOS heap implementation.

functions.name: vPortInitialiseBlocks
functions.signature: void vPortInitialiseBlocks( void )
functions.description: Initializes or resets internal heap management blocks for the FreeRTOS heap implementation (port-specific). Typically used with certain heap schemes.
requirements: Should be called before performing allocations if required by the selected heap implementation.
No parameters; must be callable at a time when heap structures can be safely reset.

functions.name: xPortGetFreeHeapSize
functions.signature: size_t xPortGetFreeHeapSize( void )
functions.description: Returns the total free heap space available (sum of all free blocks) in bytes for the current FreeRTOS heap implementation.
requirements: Heap must be initialized/configured prior to calling.

functions.name: xPortGetMinimumEverFreeHeapSize
functions.signature: size_t xPortGetMinimumEverFreeHeapSize( void )
functions.description: Returns the minimum amount of total free heap space that has remained since system start (the low-water mark), in bytes.
requirements: Heap must be initialized/configured prior to calling.

functions.name: xPortResetHeapMinimumEverFreeHeapSize
functions.signature: void xPortResetHeapMinimumEverFreeHeapSize( void )
functions.description: Resets the tracked minimum-ever-free-heap value so new low-water mark measurements start from the current state.
requirements: Call only if the port’s heap implementation supports resetting this statistic.

functions.name: pvPortMallocStack
functions.signature: void * pvPortMallocStack( size_t xSize )
functions.description: Allocates stack memory of xSize bytes from a separate stack heap when separate stack allocation is enabled.
requirements: Only available when configSTACK_ALLOCATION_FROM_SEPARATE_HEAP == 1; otherwise this name is a macro alias to pvPortMalloc.
xSize specifies the size in bytes to allocate for a stack.
Returned pointer must be freed with vPortFreeStack().
Allocation may fail; callers must handle failure (e.g., NULL return) and note that vApplicationMallocFailedHook() may be called if configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK == 1.

functions.name: vPortFreeStack
functions.signature: void vPortFreeStack( void * pv )
functions.description: Frees stack memory previously allocated by pvPortMallocStack back to the separate stack heap when enabled.
requirements: Only available when configSTACK_ALLOCATION_FROM_SEPARATE_HEAP == 1; otherwise this name is a macro alias to vPortFree.
pv must be either NULL or a pointer previously returned by pvPortMallocStack for this port.

functions.name: vPortHeapResetState
functions.signature: void vPortHeapResetState( void )
functions.description: Resets the internal state of the heap module. Intended to be called by the application before restarting the scheduler.
requirements: Must be called before restarting the scheduler.
Call only when it is safe to reset heap internal state (no outstanding allocations that must persist).

functions.name: vApplicationMallocFailedHook
functions.signature: void vApplicationMallocFailedHook( void )
functions.description: Application-defined hook that is called when a memory allocation fails in the FreeRTOS heap (if enabled). Use to log or recover from allocation failures.
requirements: Only available when configUSE_MALLOC_FAILED_HOOK == 1.
Must be provided by the application if the hook is enabled; it takes no parameters and returns void.

functions.name: xPortStartScheduler
functions.signature: BaseType_t xPortStartScheduler( void )
functions.description: Initializes the hardware/ISR tick and starts the scheduler so tasks begin executing.
requirements: Must be called to start the FreeRTOS scheduler; typically called once after system/task initialization.
Call in a context where the scheduler can take control and interrupts can be configured by the port.

functions.name: vPortEndScheduler
functions.signature: void vPortEndScheduler( void )
functions.description: Stops the scheduler and undoes hardware/ISR setup performed when starting the scheduler, returning the system to its original condition (port dependent).
requirements: Call only on ports that support ending the scheduler.
Call only after the scheduler has been started.

functions.name: vPortStoreTaskMPUSettings
functions.signature: void vPortStoreTaskMPUSettings( xMPU_SETTINGS * xMPUSettings, const struct xMEMORY_REGION * const xRegions, StackType_t * pxBottomOfStack, configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE uxStackDepth )
functions.description: Populates xMPUSettings with MPU configuration for a task based on provided memory regions and stack information. Used by the port’s MPU wrapper support.
requirements: Only available when portUSING_MPU_WRAPPERS == 1.
xMPUSettings must point to writable storage for the resulting settings.
xRegions must point to the memory region descriptors expected by the port (const input).
pxBottomOfStack must point to the bottom of the task’s stack.
uxStackDepth specifies the stack depth in units of configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE.

functions.name: xPortIsAuthorizedToAccessBuffer
functions.signature: BaseType_t xPortIsAuthorizedToAccessBuffer( const void * pvBuffer, uint32_t ulBufferLength, uint32_t ulAccessRequested )
functions.description: Checks whether the calling task is authorized to access the buffer described by pvBuffer and ulBufferLength with the requested access permissions (MPU feature). Returns pdTRUE if authorized, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: Only available when portUSING_MPU_WRAPPERS == 1.
pvBuffer must point to the buffer to check; may be NULL only if allowed by the port (unknown).
ulBufferLength is the length in bytes of the buffer.
ulAccessRequested encodes the access permissions requested; values are port-defined.
Caller must handle a pdFALSE result as lack of authorization.

functions.name: xPortIsAuthorizedToAccessKernelObject
functions.signature: BaseType_t xPortIsAuthorizedToAccessKernelObject( int32_t lInternalIndexOfKernelObject )
functions.description: Checks whether the calling task is authorized to access the kernel object identified by its internal index in the kernel object handle pool. Returns pdTRUE if authorized, pdFALSE otherwise.
requirements: Only available when portUSING_MPU_WRAPPERS == 1 and configUSE_MPU_WRAPPERS_V1 == 0.
lInternalIndexOfKernelObject must be a valid index into the kernel object handle pool as defined by the port/kernel.
Caller must handle a pdFALSE result as lack of authorization.

functions.name: MPU_vTaskDelay
functions.signature: void MPU_vTaskDelay( const TickType_t xTicksToDelay ) FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL;
functions.description: Delay/sleep the calling task for a number of tick periods. MPU wrapper around vTaskDelay to enter privileged mode, call, then return.
requirements: Must be called from task context, not from an ISR.
xTicksToDelay is in tick periods; zero yields to ready tasks.
The scheduler must be running for an actual delay.

functions.name: MPU_xTaskDelayUntil
functions.signature: BaseType_t MPU_xTaskDelayUntil( TickType_t * const pxPreviousWakeTime, const TickType_t xTimeIncrement ) FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL;
functions.description: Periodically delay a task until a fixed tick-wake schedule (absolute-delay). MPU wrapper of xTaskDelayUntil.
requirements: Must be called from task context.
pxPreviousWakeTime must be a valid, writable pointer to a TickType_t that is initialized before first call.
xTimeIncrement is the period in ticks and should be > 0.

functions.name: MPU_xTaskAbortDelay
functions.signature: BaseType_t MPU_xTaskAbortDelay( TaskHandle_t xTask ) FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL;
functions.description: Abort the Blocked state of a delayed task, readying it. MPU wrapper of xTaskAbortDelay.
requirements: xTask must be a valid task handle.
May be called from task or ISR context as per underlying API; check return value for success.

functions.name: MPU_uxTaskPriorityGet
functions.signature: UBaseType_t MPU_uxTaskPriorityGet( const TaskHandle_t xTask ) FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL;
functions.description: Get a task's current priority. MPU wrapper of uxTaskPriorityGet.
requirements: xTask may be NULL to query the calling task, or a valid task handle.

functions.name: MPU_eTaskGetState
functions.signature: eTaskState MPU_eTaskGetState( TaskHandle_t xTask ) FREERTOS_SYSTEM_CALL;

functions.name: MPU_xTaskCreate

functions.description: Create a new task. MPU wrapper that allows using opaque handles with privilege mediation.
requirements: pxTaskCode must be a valid task entry function.
pcName must be a valid string pointer or NULL (name length subject to configMAX_TASK_NAME_LEN).
uxStackDepth is the stack size in words (type configSTACK_DEPTH_TYPE).
pvParameters is passed to the created task and may be NULL.
uxPriority must be within valid priority range per configuration.
pxCreatedTask may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive the created task handle.

requirements: pxTaskCode must be a valid task entry function.
pcName must be a valid string pointer or NULL per config.
uxStackDepth is stack size in words and must match supplied stack buffer size.
puxStackBuffer must point to caller-allocated stack storage; not NULL.
pxTaskBuffer must point to caller-allocated StaticTask_t; not NULL.
uxPriority within valid range.

functions.name: Atomic_CompareAndSwap_u32
functions.signature: static portFORCE_INLINE uint32_t Atomic_CompareAndSwap_u32( uint32_t volatile * pulDestination, uint32_t ulExchange, uint32_t ulComparand )
functions.description: Atomically compares *pulDestination with ulComparand and, if equal, stores ulExchange into *pulDestination. Returns 1 on successful swap, 0 otherwise. Intended for lock-free state updates using global interrupt masking on FreeRTOS ports.
requirements: pulDestination must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a uint32_t object accessible in the current context.
The pointed object should be naturally aligned for uint32_t per target ABI.
Operation is atomic with respect to tasks; it is safe in ISRs only on ports where portHAS_NESTED_INTERRUPTS == 1; must not be used in ISRs when portHAS_NESTED_INTERRUPTS == 0.
The operation uses 32-bit unsigned arithmetic/compare semantics.
Include FreeRTOS.h before including atomic.h as required by the header.

functions.description: Atomically swaps the pointer stored at *ppvDestination with pvExchange. Returns the previous pointer value. Useful for exchanging references under interrupt masking.
requirements: ppvDestination must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to a pointer-sized object (void*) accessible in the current context.
The pointed location should be naturally aligned for a pointer per target ABI.
Operation is atomic with respect to tasks; it is safe in ISRs only on ports where portHAS_NESTED_INTERRUPTS == 1; must not be used in ISRs when portHAS_NESTED_INTERRUPTS == 0.
Returned value is the original *ppvDestination prior to the swap.
Include FreeRTOS.h before including atomic.h as required by the header.

functions.description: Atomically compares the pointer at *ppvDestination with pvComparand and, if equal, stores pvExchange. Returns 1 if the swap occurred, 0 otherwise. Intended for pointer-sized CAS under interrupt masking.

functions.name: vApplicationStackOverflowHook
functions.signature: void vApplicationStackOverflowHook( TaskHandle_t xTask, char * pcTaskName );
functions.description: Application-defined hook that FreeRTOS calls when a task’s stack is detected to have overflowed (or likely overflowed) during a context switch. Intended for logging, fault handling, or system recovery. This function is referenced by taskCHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW() macros in this header but must be implemented by the application elsewhere.
requirements: The function must be provided by the application when stack overflow checking is enabled (configCHECK_FOR_STACK_OVERFLOW > 0).
Parameter xTask must be a valid TaskHandle_t referring to the task being checked (the kernel passes the current TCB).
Parameter pcTaskName is expected to point to a NUL-terminated task name string; do not dereference it if it is NULL (defensive handling recommended).

The hook should avoid blocking or calling API functions that might assume a valid running task context, as it may be invoked during a context switch; keep it short and re-entrant if used across tasks/ISRs.
No return value; any error handling or system reaction must be performed inside the hook.

functions.name: memcmp
functions.signature: int memcmp( const void * s1, const void * s2, size_t n );
functions.description: Compares the first n bytes of the memory areas s1 and s2. Returns <0, 0, or >0 depending on whether s1 is lexicographically less than, equal to, or greater than s2. Standard C library function; referenced here to check a known fill pattern at the end of a task’s stack.
requirements: If n > 0, s1 must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
If n > 0, s2 must point to a readable memory region of at least n bytes.
It is permissible for s1 or s2 to be NULL only when n == 0 (no bytes are accessed).
No overlap requirements (overlap is allowed since only reads occur), but both regions must be accessible for reading.
Return value handling: negative if s1 < s2, zero if equal, positive if s1 > s2 (byte-wise comparison using unsigned char semantics).

functions.name: vPortYield
functions.signature: void vPortYield( void );
functions.description: Requests a context switch/yield in the FreeRTOS port. Typically used by the scheduler, ISRs via macros, or tasks to relinquish the CPU.
requirements: Should be called only when the FreeRTOS scheduler/port is initialized and running (exact conditions not specified in this header).
From ISRs, use the provided macros portYIELD_FROM_ISR/portEND_SWITCHING_ISR to invoke a yield safely (inferred from macros defined in this header).

functions.name: vPortDisableInterrupts
functions.signature: void vPortDisableInterrupts( void );
functions.description: Disables interrupts for the current context according to the port’s interrupt model. Used to begin a critical section or prevent preemption/ISR execution.
requirements: If used directly, ensure interrupts are subsequently re-enabled to avoid system lockup (general requirement for disable/enable pairs; exact policy not specified here).
Prefer using portSET_INTERRUPT_MASK()/portCLEAR_INTERRUPT_MASK() or portENTER_CRITICAL()/portEXIT_CRITICAL() macros for portability and correct semantics (implied by macro wrappers in this header).

functions.name: vPortEnableInterrupts
functions.signature: void vPortEnableInterrupts( void );
functions.description: Enables interrupts for the current context according to the port’s interrupt model. Complements vPortDisableInterrupts and ends an interrupt-disabled region.
requirements: Call only after interrupts have been disabled or masked if the intention is to restore normal operation (pairing implied).
Prefer using portCLEAR_INTERRUPT_MASK() or portEXIT_CRITICAL() macros when matching higher-level operations (implied by macro wrappers).

functions.name: xPortSetInterruptMask
functions.signature: UBaseType_t xPortSetInterruptMask( void );
functions.description: Masks/blocks interrupts as defined by the port and returns the previous interrupt mask/state so it can be restored later. Used for ISR-safe critical sections.
requirements: The returned mask value must be preserved and later passed to vPortClearInterruptMask to restore the prior state (implied by portSET/CLEAR_INTERRUPT_MASK_FROM_ISR macros).
Use this function in contexts where an ISR-safe mask/restore pattern is required (e.g., within ISRs), typically via portSET_INTERRUPT_MASK_FROM_ISR().

functions.name: vPortClearInterruptMask
functions.signature: void vPortClearInterruptMask( UBaseType_t xMask );
functions.description: Restores the interrupt mask/state previously returned by xPortSetInterruptMask, re-enabling interrupts to their prior level.
requirements: xMask must be a value previously returned by xPortSetInterruptMask from the same context.
Do not pass arbitrary values; using an incorrect mask may leave interrupts in an unintended state.

functions.name: vPortEnterCritical
functions.signature: void vPortEnterCritical( void );
functions.description: Enters a critical section by disabling interrupts in a way suitable for task-level protection on this port. Pairs with vPortExitCritical.
requirements: Must be paired with a matching vPortExitCritical call in the same task/context.
Nesting behavior is not documented here; avoid unmatched or cross-task use.
Use the portENTER_CRITICAL() macro to invoke this function for portability.

functions.name: vPortExitCritical
functions.signature: void vPortExitCritical( void );
functions.description: Exits a critical section previously entered by vPortEnterCritical, restoring the prior interrupt state.
requirements: Must match a prior vPortEnterCritical call in the same task/context.
Do not call without a corresponding enter; doing so may incorrectly enable interrupts.

functions.name: vPortThreadDying
functions.signature: void vPortThreadDying( void * pxTaskToDelete, volatile BaseType_t * pxPendYield );
functions.description: Port-specific hook invoked before a task is deleted (via portPRE_TASK_DELETE_HOOK). Performs cleanup and can request a yield by setting the provided flag.
requirements: pxTaskToDelete must reference the task being deleted (type is opaque here; provided as void*).
pxPendYield must be a valid, non-null pointer to a BaseType_t flag that the port may modify to indicate a pending yield.
Intended to be called via the portPRE_TASK_DELETE_HOOK macro rather than directly.

functions.name: vPortCancelThread
functions.signature: void vPortCancelThread( void * pxTaskToDelete );
functions.description: Port-specific cleanup invoked when a task’s TCB is being cleaned up (via portCLEAN_UP_TCB). Cancels/destroys the underlying OS thread resources for the task.
requirements: pxTaskToDelete must reference a valid task control block or port-specific task handle associated with the task being cleaned up (opaque type here; provided as void*).
